10038635:
Testimony in Support of LD 775: "An Act Requiring Voter Approval of Legislative and Gubernatorial Pay Increases"
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and the distinguished members of the Committee On State and Local Government, my name is Harris Van Pate, and I serve as policy analyst for Maine Policy Institute. Maine Policy is a free market think tank, a nonpartisan, non-profit organization that advocates for individual liberty and economic freedom in Maine. Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony support for LD 775, "An Act Requiring Voter Approval of Legislative and Gubernatorial Pay Increases."
Public service is a noble calling, and those who serve as elected officials deserve fair compensation. However, determining these salaries must be transparent, accountable, and ultimately reflective of the people's will. LD 775 ensures that any future increases in the wages of Maine's governor, senators, and representatives are subject to voter approval, reinforcing a critical principle of democratic governance: elected officials should not have unilateral authority to raise their salaries without direct input from the taxpayers who fund them.
Under current law, legislators and the governor can approve salary increases without a direct mechanism for voter oversight. This practice raises legitimate concerns about self-dealing and conflicts of interest. The passage of LD 775 would provide an essential safeguard by requiring that any legislative or gubernatorial salary increase be placed on the ballot at the next general election, allowing Maine voters to determine whether such increases are warranted.
Furthermore, requiring voter approval of salary increases would encourage elected officials to consider when and why such increases are proposed more carefully. This added level of accountability fosters trust in government and ensures that salary decisions are made with the best interests of Maine taxpayers in mind.
Maine voters deserve a say in spending their tax dollars, particularly when compensating their elected officials. By supporting LD 775, the Legislature can take a meaningful step toward restoring public confidence in state government and ensuring that salary decisions reflect the people's will.
For these reasons, I strongly urge the committee to support LD 775. Thank you for your time and consideration.

In Opposition to LD 775, An Act Requiring Voter Approval of Legislative and Gubernatorial Pay Increases
Senator Joseph Baldacci, Representative Suzanne Salisbury and honorable members of the State and Local Government Committee . I am Joyce A. Maker from Calais, Maine. I in opposition of LD 775.
As a prior legislator, I disagree with this bill because of the politics of it. Most do not want to vote on their own raise (and can't because of the constitution) and that is why they make it for the next legislative term and the case of the Governor that position will not get a raise until the new Governor is voted in. It should not be voted by the people because they are a Republican, Democrat or Independent, it should be raised if their salary is below standard like the Governor's pay is now compared to other Governors. "In 2023, US governors' salaries ranged from a low of $70,000 in Maine to a high of $250,000 in New York, with most earning at least $100,000 annually. Here's a more detailed breakdown: Highest Paid: New York at $250,000. Lowest Paid: Maine at $70,000." https://ballotpedia.org/Comparison_of_gubernatorial_salaries

I know the days and hours I put in as a legislator when we were not in session but your still on duty and have obligations and receive no pay.
Thank you in advance for your consideration on such a serious matter. Please vote ought not to pass on all these bill.
Sincerely,

Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, Distinguished Colleagues of the State and Local Government Committee:
l am still Will Tuell. I still represent House District 10, which consists of nearly two dozen small communities in central and coastal Washington County, and I am
here today to enthusiastically present LD 775, "An Act Requiring Voter Approval of Legislative and Gubernatorial Pay lncreases."
This bill does exactly what the title says. Under it, any pay raises outside of a
COLA that we approve for future lawmakers and governors would be put out to
the public for their consideration.

I say this with nothing but appreciation and respect for the hard decision the 131$`
Legislature made in approving significant pay raises for lawmakers and the chief
"
executive.
In my nine years of serving, l know all too well the challenges many of you
grappled with in passing those raises.
On one hand, lawmakers do put in crazy hours working with constituents, drafting
bills, trying to educate themselves on issues, and serving their constituents. The same is true of the Chief Executive.
On the other hand, constituents are struggling with inflation, housing, caring for
their loved ones, groceries, their property taxes, running their small businesses,
and getting the healthcare they need.
Whether you voted for last year's pay raise or not, whether you would have (or not) if you weren't here, the pros and cons are real, and they are not black and
white.
That is exactly why we should be putting those raises out to the voters instead of
passing them without voters consent.
l am not one who believes "we're voting ourselves a pay raise" because l know
that raise only goes into effect with the next legislature or the next governor, but
that really isn't the point.

House District 10

The public, the people we represent, should have the final say on what we, and those who come after us, those who come after the next chief executive, are
paid.
If we believe it's important that pay should be raised, we should not have an problem whatsoever putting it out to the people who have entrusted us with these
seats.
"But," you may be thinking, "the public doesn't know how much work this job is." I agree. But I also believe we are capable of giving our constituents, the general public, the information to make an informed decision should they be asked to do
so.
l also have faith that they will make the choice that is best for themselves, their families, and their communities. They may agree that the raise is warranted and support it. They may not. Either way, we need to put our faith and trust in them
because they have put theirs in us to represent their interests.
I also believe that if we handled future pay raises for lawmakers and the governor In this way that more modest proposals would emerge as a result. Lawmakers
would not be putting in bills for double digit pay increases for fear the public
would reject them, and the onus would be on us to explain to the public why such
a raise is warranted.
Beyond all that, we would not be "voting ourselves" a raise in the eyes of the public. They would be voting us a raise, and I think we would, or certainly should,
have more appreciation for it if the voters consented. Thank you, and I would be happy to take any questions.
House District 10
